title: Accounting for Non-Accountants
overview: Accounting is often referred to as the language of business. This course is designed to provide participants with a solid foundation in accounting principles, including how to read and analyze financial statements. Participants will gain an understanding of the relationship between accounting and finance, the mechanics of debits and credits, and the skills needed to accurately record financial transactions and summarize them in financial statements.
audience: This course is ideal for managers, supervisors, and staff from various functions, including those in the accounting department, who wish to enhance their understanding of accounting principles and techniques.
methodology: This course employs a blend of interactive learning techniques, including concise presentations, participant-led discussions, and hands-on exercises. Real-life case studies are a key feature, allowing participants to apply theoretical knowledge to practical scenarios and present their solutions.
competencies: Preparing income statements and interpreting balance sheets
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Explain the purpose of accounting and the accounting cycle.
Identify key accounting principles and rules under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).
Demonstrate knowledge of the accounting equation, double-entry bookkeeping, and automated accounting systems.
Recognize the primary financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, statement of changes in equity, and cash flow statement) and their components.
Apply adjustments to financial statements at month-end and year-end.

outline.title: 1. Introduction to Accounting and Financial Statements

items.text: Understanding corporate entities and presentation of financial information
Role of the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB)
Differences between IFRS and US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP)
The accounting equation and its components
Understanding assets, liabilities, and equity relationships
The chart of accounts, general journal, general ledger, and trial balance
Definition and purpose of income statements
Calculating profits: gross, operating, and net
Definition of capital stock and retained earnings
Distinctions between cash dividends, stock dividends, and stock splits
Purpose and structure of the balance sheet
Differentiating between current and non-current items
Definition and purpose of the cash flow statement
Illustrated examples of cash flow statements
Accounting for depreciation, bad debts, and provisions for contingencies
